output.brief: Most likely cause: water-contaminated brake fluid from one bulk drum at Northfield Motor Services, used for 11 of the 13 Eastgate vans serviced there while the in-house bay was closed. The two vans that got fluid from a new drum are the only exceptions. Two vans came back on 24 Sep with a long pedal on hills. Their fluid boiled at 152°C and 149°C, against 255°C for sealed stock. Renewing the fluid fixed those two. Northfield warned Larkspur on 25 Sep to recheck the other vans, and nobody replied. The same drivers report no problems in other vans on the same hills, so technique and the Upper Wend routes are not the cause. Tessaro pads were fitted at both garages and in-house, and the complaints follow the vans serviced at Northfield, so the pads are not the cause. I'm fairly sure of this, though I haven't tested the other vans' fluid. Next: pull the Northfield-serviced vans, test and renew their fluid from sealed stock, and keep them off hills until that is done. Do not discipline drivers. Their reports were accurate and discouraging reports is dangerous. Keep the pad switch as a separate issue.
